hardcodedGaps: Scrollbar geometry is hardcoded, not variable-driven. Only the three colors (--scrollbar-thumb-bg, --scrollbar-thumb-bg-hover, --scrollbar-track-bg) are tokens. In features/theme/styles/Scroller.module.css the track width/height is a literal 1rem (L10-13), the thumb min-height is 2.5rem (L21), the thumb/track inset border is 0.25rem solid transparent with border-radius 0.5rem (L42-47), and .scrollerWithBottomGutter adds a literal 0.5rem margin (L29). A channel theme can recolor the scrollbar but cannot resize or reshape it.

Avatar shape is not themeable. The circular crop is a literal border-radius: 50% in features/ui/components/BaseAvatar.module.css (L22, .overlay) and features/ui/avatars/AvatarStack.module.css (L24, L32). No avatar-shape token exists anywhere, so a channel theme cannot make avatars squared or rounded-rect. Only --message-avatar-size / --message-avatar-size-compact (size, not shape) are exposed.

Avatar status-badge and mask variables exist in CSS but are absent from the manifest. features/ui/components/BaseAvatar.module.css consumes --avatar-status-radius (L47), --avatar-mask-cx / --avatar-mask-x / --avatar-mask-width (L69-71), --avatar-status-right / -bottom / -width / -height (L40-45). These are never declared in any CSS file; they are written as inline styles from BaseAvatar.tsx (see the typed style keys at L40 and the assignment at L231). Inline styles on the avatar element beat an inherited channel-scope value, so overriding them from a channel theme would not work even if they were surfaced.

Avatar transition timing is hardcoded outside the manifest. --avatar-status-transition-duration (160ms) and --avatar-status-transition-easing (ease-out) are declared on the .container component class in features/ui/components/BaseAvatar.module.css (L5-6), not on :root, so the manifest generator never sees them. They also do not reuse --transition-fast/normal/slow.

The manifest generator only reads :root and .theme-light declaration blocks (scripts/GenerateThemeVariables.ts, readSourceVariables - it skips every block whose selector is neither, L174-179). Any custom property declared on a component class is structurally invisible to the manifest. This is the root cause of the avatar gaps above and is a general blind spot, not a one-off omission.

The manifest models only two themes, but four exist. features/theme/styles/generated/color-system.css defines :root (dark, L3), .theme-light (L190), .theme-coal (L324) and .theme-dark_legacy (L427). THEME_STUDIO_DARK/LIGHT_DEFAULT_VARIABLE_VALUES cover only the first two, so for a user on coal or dark_legacy the editor default shown next to a control will not match what they actually see.

--saturation-factor is inert when set at channel scope. Every color in color-system.css bakes var(--saturation-factor) into its own declared value on :root (e.g. --background-primary: hsl(258, calc(10% * var(--saturation-factor)), 5%)). Per the CSS custom-property spec, var() inside a custom property is substituted at computed-value time on the element the declaration applies to, so descendants inherit an already-substituted color. Overriding --saturation-factor inside [data-channel-theme-id] therefore affects only declarations written in that same scope, not the inherited palette. It is in the manifest but effectively a no-op for a channel theme.

--textarea-horizontal-padding has a malformed default value in the manifest: "1rem)" with an unbalanced closing paren (ThemeVariableManifest.ts L1166 and L1502). The real source is --textarea-horizontal-padding: var(--chat-horizontal-padding, var(--spacing-4)) (features/channel/components/textarea/TextareaInput.module.css L16). The generator regex for var() fallbacks is /var\(\s*(--[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)(?:\s*,\s*([^)]+))?\)/g - the [^)]+ fallback group stops at the first closing paren, so a nested var() fallback is truncated and leaves a stray ")". This is the only malformed value of the 333 (verified by a paren-balance scan over both maps); the true runtime value is 1rem. An editor seeding a control from this default would emit invalid CSS.

--textarea-side-button-padding and --typing-upload-column-width use a unitless zero inside max() alongside lengths: max( 0, calc((2.5rem - 2.25rem) / 2) ). CSS math functions require consistent argument types, so a bare <number> against a <length> is invalid at computed-value time. This is the same bug class the repo already fixed elsewhere (commit dbe38255, "fix(app): unitless zero fallback in voice calc"). Source: features/channel/components/textarea/TextareaInput.module.css L19-22 and src/app/globals.css L115-118.

Markdown code blocks use the wrong scrollbar tokens. features/theme/styles/Markup.module.css L307 sets scrollbar-color: var(--background-tertiary) var(--background-primary) instead of --scrollbar-thumb-bg / --scrollbar-track-bg, so retheming the scrollbar colors leaves code-block scrollbars on the surface palette.

Transition durations are hardcoded at many channel-scope sites even though --transition-fast/normal/slow exist: GuildMembersPage.module.css L222, L263, L600; ChannelAttachmentArea.module.css L84; MessageAttachments.module.css L66; EmojiPicker.module.css L50, L242; GifPicker.module.css L185, L200, L322; ScheduledMessageEditBar.module.css L36; MemesPicker.module.css L33. Motion is therefore only partially themeable.

Hardcoded colors inside the channel content area, all non-tokenised and therefore not retheamable: ChannelAttachmentArea.module.css L66, L80, L88, L103, L270, L282; MemesPicker.module.css L146, L200, L206; PremiumUpsellBanner.module.css L31, L36, L39, L57; MemberListItem.module.css L121 (owner crown, hsl(39, 57%, 64%)); RecipientRemoveMessage.module.css L4; GuildJoinMessage.module.css L4; ChannelReplyBar.module.css L48; ChannelSearchHighlight.css L4 (search hit highlight, rgba(255, 230, 0, 0.25)); ChannelIndexPage.module.css L9, L15, L38, L62 and direct_message/DirectMessageLayout.module.css L22, L45, L57 (literal #000 backgrounds).

Portal-rendered surfaces escape the channel scope entirely. Modals, popouts, tooltips, toasts, bottom sheets, the media viewer, the expression picker and the mobile SelectMode overlay all render via createPortal into document.body (features/ui/popover/PopoverPopouts.tsx, features/ui/toast/Toasts.tsx, features/ui/sheet/Sheet.tsx, features/messaging/components/modals/MediaViewerModal.tsx, features/expressions/components/popouts/ExpressionPickerPopout.tsx, features/channel/components/channel_view/GuildChannelView.tsx L336). They are not descendants of the themed <main>, so no channel-scoped override reaches them - including every --z-index-* variable.

Sixteen app-shell variables are present in the manifest but unreachable from a channel theme, because they are consumed only outside <main>: --layout-sidebar-width, --layout-guild-list-width, --guild-icon-size, --guild-icon-gap, --layout-user-area-height, --layout-user-area-reserved-height, --user-area-content-height, --user-area-padding-x, --user-area-padding-y, --user-area-divider-color, --native-titlebar-height, --mobile-bottom-nav-height, --layout-mobile-bottom-nav-reserved-height, --footer-row-height, --footer-row-padding-y, --layout-header-popout-width. Verified by tracing var() consumers into features/app/components/layout/ and features/guild/components/popouts/. They are marked edge-case here and should be hidden or disabled in the editor rather than offered as working controls.

Eight variables are written as inline styles on document.documentElement by useThemeCssVariables (features/theme/hooks/useThemeCssVariables.ts L30-46): --saturation-factor, --user-select, --font-size, --chat-horizontal-padding, --message-group-spacing, --link-decoration, --markup-strikethrough-color, plus the non-custom dynamic-range-limit. A channel-scope declaration on a descendant still wins for that subtree, so these remain overridable - but they are bound to the user accessibility settings (font size, message gutter, group spacing, link underline, text selection). Overriding them in a channel theme silently overrides a per-user accessibility preference inside that channel.
excludedNote: Variables flagged `excluded` generate no editor control. --saturation-factor is inert at channel scope (colors bake it in at computed-value time on :root, so descendants inherit already-substituted values); --z-index-* carry no visual token and are deferred from the first control pass.
